title: Correct publish push copy progress
summary: Correct publish push progress when Robocopy/SMB preallocates the destination file to the final size before bytes finish transferring.
reason: The Push file bar could show 100%, ETA 0s, and write 0 B/s immediately after a push began because destination file length was treated as completed copy progress.
behavior_before: During an active Robocopy push, a preallocated landed file with final length could make CopyBytesCopied equal CopyTotalBytes before the network transfer completed.
behavior_after: During an active Robocopy push, final-size landed file length is treated as preallocation and progress uses process write I/O estimates when available, only reporting 100% after Robocopy exits.
rollback_plan: Revert the Robocopy active-copy telemetry estimator and related tests. Existing publish copy and pending-publish file movement remain unchanged.
notes:
Follow-up to the publish ETA UI change after live SMB copy evidence showed the landed file size can jump to full size at copy start.
Robocopy active-copy progress now treats full-size landed files as possible SMB preallocation and estimates progress from process write counters when available.
Validation note: broad WebView static/browser suites currently have unrelated dirty-worktree failures outside this storage telemetry fix.
Implemented and validated on 2026-06-04; active Robocopy polls no longer trust full-size landed files as complete copy progress.
